analysis:
Both units are head_text excerpts of docs/provider/cli-reference.md (modified, mode 100644 on base and head). No patch or base text was supplied, so the exact changed lines cannot be identified. The content is operator documentation, not code.

Cache section (lines 18-40) is consistent with T-041:
- Selected directory pins the volume UUID; payloads live under darkbloom/kv3.
- Invalid or changed storage disables the SSD tier, and inference continues cold.
- The text explicitly disclaims firmware certification.
- The saved daily write limit takes precedence over the env var, which only affects the endurance guard, not the 30-minute TTL bound.

Logout section (lines 448-487) matches the A-008/T-053 description:
- Revocation goes to the recorded issuer, not to --config.
- Only HTTP 204 confirms revocation; there are no redirects and a 10s timeout.
- Offline logout is local-only, and tokens are not logged.

Other sections:
- Restart (823, 835-836) says self_route authorization is not public-fleet eligibility, consistent with T-052.
- Enroll (557-569) says the OS choice grants no authorization (T-052/T-057).
- The macOS<27 upgrade notice (54-62) performs no network or config operations.
- The native serve qualification diagnostic (44-52) is hidden, env-gated and restricted to 127.0.0.1 transport.

No security regression or threat-model contradiction is visible in the documentation. Next pass: the documented behavior should be verified against source (CacheConfiguration.swift updateCacheSettings, ProviderLogout.swift revokeToken, NativeServeQualificationCommand.swift), because doc claims alone do not prove implementation.
